findings.title: Indefinite-length ASN.1 encoding (-1) is not rejected and causes NegativeArraySizeException or silent truncation
findings.body: `ASN1Decoder.readLength()` returns `-1` when it encounters `0x80` (indefinite-length encoding). However, callers (`readSequence`, `readInteger`, `readNext`) do not check for `-1`. In `readInteger`, passing `-1` to `read(-1)` allocates `new byte[-1]` and throws `NegativeArraySizeException` instead of an `IOException`. In `readSequence`, `length` is `-1` so `while (length > 0)` immediately terminates and returns an empty sequence. In `readNext`, `length += reset()` adds the header byte count to `-1`, reading a truncated slice of bytes. Since ECDSA signatures must be DER-encoded (which forbids indefinite lengths), `readLength()` should throw an `IOException` when `length == 0x80` (or when `length < 0`).

findings.title: Dead ASN1Encoder allocations in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard both results before repeating the exact same calls on lines 119-120 inside `writeDerSeq(...)`. Those two statements are dead work and should be removed.

findings.title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses a single P-256 key for ES256, ES384, and ES512 and does not verify the re-encoded DER signature
findings.body: `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` generates a single default EC `KeyPair` (256-bit P-256) in the constructor and reuses it across `testES256`, `testES384`, and `testES512`. Signing with `SHA384withECDSA` or `SHA512withECDSA` using a P-256 key still produces ~32-byte `r` and `s` values, while `algorithm.getSignatureLength()` is 96 for ES384 and 132 for ES512. As a result, full-size 48-byte (P-384) and 66-byte (P-521, which also exercises DER lengths > 127 bytes) `r` and `s` integers are never tested. In addition, the test never verifies `asn1Des` with `Signature.verify(asn1Des)` (or `Assert.assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des)`), so a bug that produces invalid DER in `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` that `ASN1Decoder` happens to accept would pass the test.

findings.title: Unparameterized logger.debugf call with dynamic string
findings.body: On line 69, `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a dynamically built string as the format pattern to `debugf` with no format arguments. Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` or `logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)` instead.
